messages:
jonathan: Heads-up — planning a patch rollout for release branch v1.12 this afternoon during the 18:00 UTC change window. Need quick consensus on tag strategy and whether we should pin the runtime dependency in the patch.

maria: What's the exact bump? patch -> 1.12.3?

sam: Yep, 1.12.3. bugfix + hotfix for grpc healthcheck. Non-breaking. The question is whether we append build meta (e.g. 1.12.3+hotfix2026) or keep it simple.

harper: We try to avoid buildmeta for prod tags — deploybot only recognizes tags matching ^v\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+$. Adding +meta often trips the release tooling.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: tag v1.12.3 queued by @jonathan — CI pipeline: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234 (running).

tia: If the runtime-proto change is the cause, can we pin runtime-proto to 2.8.1 inside the patch? Pinning might be fastest to stabilize.

maria: I'd avoid pinning transitive runtime deps in patches unless absolutely necessary. Pinning can force consumers to upgrade unexpectedly. Consider a tiny shim or revert instead.

jonathan: Agreed — don't pin. We'll include a minimal compatibility shim in the patch and call it out in the changelog. Also we should document the backport branch used.

sam: For tagging convention: use annotated tag `v1.12.3` and include a clear tag message with `cherry-pick: release/1.12` + CI run id. Keeps deploybot happy and gives traceability. Example tag message:

```
Release v1.12.3
cherry-pick: release/1.12
ci: 1234
notes: fix grpc healthcheck race
```

harper: I'll update the release notes template to add a "backport" field and a short "compat shim" entry. Also will add `--no-buildmeta` to the tag script so accidental buildmeta is excluded.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: CI passed for v1.12.3, canary rollout started in us-west-2. Notifying @oncall for 30m monitoring.

tia: :thumbsup: I'll monitor. Rollback policy reminder: rollback to v1.12.2 if errors >1% or p95 latency increases >150ms for the service.

jonathan: Cool — proceeding with v1.12.3 annotated tag and canary. I'll post the release note once the canary is green. Thanks all.
